_note: Single source of truth. No exam name, legal string, scale value, threshold or policy number is ever hand-typed in backend or UI code. Everything reads from here. Adding an exam = a new object under 'exams' + (only if its aggregation maths is genuinely new) a new strategy. v2 replaces the 'skills' array with 'components', and splits scale / component / aggregation into three orthogonal concepts so that non-language exams (GRE, GMAT) fit without a rewrite.
_v2_changes: skills -> components. A component is any assessable or practisable unit. Modality (reading/listening/writing/speaking/quantitative/integrated) is an optional TAG, not the organising rule.
scales extracted to a reusable top-level block. A component references a scale by id.
overall.mode added: aggregate | per_component. Three of the five exams here have NO computable headline score - this is a fact about the exams, not a gap.
surface_only removed - superseded by assessed:true|false. One mechanism, not two.
remediation added at component, subskill and item_tag level, by content reference (never embedded URLs).
variants added (IELTS Academic/General Training, OET's 12 professions).
defaults block added for platform-wide policy; exams may override.
legal block extended with machine-checkable usage constraints.
progression reworked: headline vs momentum separated so the invariant is satisfiable.

defaults._note: Platform-wide policy. An exam may override any key. Founder-confirmed Aug 2026.

attempts._note: Scheduled assessments only. Missing the window forfeits the attempt; there is no retake. Practice and drills are unlimited and ungraded.

unlock_requirement._note: or_all_scheduled_in_window exists so a student in an institute that schedules fewer than 6 IAs a month is not permanently locked out through no fault of their own. Unlock = completed >= min(6, scheduled_in_window).

full_mock._entitlement_note: If a mock is unlocked but unused when the window rolls, does the entitlement lapse or carry? Unanswered. Default until decided: lapse.

graded_attempts._b2c_gap: TBD_FOUNDER — school_strict assumes someone schedules the assessments. Self-serve B2C students have no scheduler, so no IA is ever 'missed' and the full mock never unlocks. Either (a) B2C students self-schedule into a fixed cadence, or (b) B2C overrides retake_policy to 'self_paced'. Build the override field now; decide before B2C launch.

scheduling._note: Month/window boundaries must resolve in a declared timezone or a student in a different timezone forfeits early. src/lib/timezone.ts already exists - use it.

baseline.note_to_student: Your diagnostic is intentionally tough — it's your starting benchmark, not your ceiling. Everything from here is real, earned improvement.

display._trend_note: Trend must compare like with like. An IA and a full mock are different instruments with different difficulty; mixing them in one 3-point window measures instrument, not progress.

progression._improvement_note: Improvement since baseline is computed on the UNCLAMPED assessed value, then displayed. If it were computed on the clamped reported value, a student moving from a true 3.0 to a true 4.5 would show +0.5 instead of +1.5 — the report_floor would eat exactly the signal this layer exists to show.

result_provenance._note: Every stored result records the engine_version and config_version it was scored under. Without this, the post-calibration threshold change silently rewrites history and every trend line becomes meaningless. Non-negotiable before the first CEFR result is stored.

scales._note: Reusable scale definitions. A component references one by id. Adding an exam whose components use an existing scale requires no new scale and no new code.

ielts_band._proficiency_note: A/B/C proficiency level + drill difficulty cuts (even thirds of [4,9], decision D3) and the weakness-gap domain (D4, gap 1.0 at 4.0 → 0.0 at 9.0). Values equal src/lib/bandScale.ts (bandToLevel/bandToDifficulty/bandGap) exactly; parity-asserted in vectors.check.ts §9. These are cut scores — stripped by toPublicConfig, never shipped to the client.
ielts_band._official_range_note: The official IELTS scale is 1.0–9.0. report_floor 4.0 is a deliberate product choice: genuine sub-4.0 performances display as 4.0. min is kept at 0.0 internally so the floor can be lowered in config without a code change.

cefr_6._threshold_provenance: Derived from Pearson's published Global Scale of English -> CEFR mapping (GSE 10–90: below A1 10–21, A1 22–29, A2 30–42, B1 43–58, B2 59–75, C1 76–84, C2 85–90), converted by pct = (GSE - 10) / 80 * 100. Every value here is that formula applied to the level's minimum GSE. PROVISIONAL — see EE-04 calibration protocol.
cefr_6._threshold_correction_note: v1 used 0/14/24/41/59/79/93. Those do not match the stated GSE derivation: B2 was 2.25 points low and C1 was 3.5 points low, which moves a real boundary. Corrected here.
cefr_6._borrowed_alignment_warning: These boundaries import Pearson's alignment of GSE to CEFR (itself anchored to North 2000). Using them means borrowing a vendor's alignment claim rather than making our own. Defensible as a starting point, NOT as a calibration. Replace after the study in EE-04.

oet_500._provenance: oet.com/test/after-the-test — 0–500 in ten-point increments, letter grade A–E per sub-test. Bands in force since the September 2018 scoring change.
oet_500._band_tiling_note: The bands look non-contiguous (B tops at 440, C+ starts at 300) but they tile exactly because the scale increments in 10s. Validator must assert tiling AT THE SCALE STEP, not at 1.

gre_section._provenance: ETS — Verbal Reasoning and Quantitative Reasoning, 130–170 in 1-point increments.

gre_analytical_writing._provenance: ETS — Analytical Writing, 0–6 in half-point increments.

gmat_section._provenance: mba.com — Quantitative Reasoning, Verbal Reasoning and Data Insights each 60–90 in 1-point intervals.

gmat_total._computable_note: GMAC does not publish the Total Score formula. It is a proprietary scaled composite of three IRT-scaled section scores, not a sum or a mean — three sections of 60–90 sum to 180–270 and average to 60–90, neither of which maps to 205–805. This scale is declared so a real GMAT score can be STORED and displayed if a student enters one. It must never be computed by this engine.

components.label: Speaking
components._subskill_provenance: CEFR Companion Volume (2020), Appendix 3 — 'Qualitative features of spoken language, expanded with phonology'. NOTE: cite Appendix 3, not Table 3. The main Table 3 in both the 2001 CEFR and the Companion Volume carries FIVE criteria; Phonology is the sixth column added only in Appendix 3.
components._subskill_caveat: These are level-descriptive bands, not a scoring rubric. Using them as rubric dimensions is legitimate but each dimension must then be validated separately — per-dimension agreement, not just overall. See EE-04.

overall._confirmed: Founder-confirmed: the headline Spoken English CEFR level is driven by the Speaking component alone. Listening, Reading and Writing are practice surfaces (assessed:false) — present in the product, absent from the headline. Changing this later is one line: add component ids to overall.components and set assessed:true.

viva._applies_to: Derived from components[].delivery == 'viva' plus modules[].speaking_delivery. The v1 field 'applies_to_modules' duplicated that and is removed — two sources of truth for the same fact is how they drift.

rules._baseline_note: The diagnostic must compute the baseline using the SAME overall.components rule as a live assessment (speaking only). If the diagnostic averages all four components while assessments average one, improvement_since_baseline compares two different quantities and every number in the progression layer is wrong.

naming._naming_note: Deliberately does NOT put 'OET' in the product name. See legal below — this is the one exam in the set where the rights holder publishes no nominative-use carve-out.

legal._risk_note: CBLA's published IP policy states its marks 'cannot be used without the prior express written permission of CBLA', and the Terms & Conditions state 'You are not permitted to use any trade marks, logos or trade names appearing on the Website.' Unlike ETS, CBLA publishes NO nominative-use or fair-use carve-out for preparation providers. It instead runs a paid Preparation Provider Programme whose Premium tier grants an official logo. This is materially more restrictive than the IELTS position. Treat 'can we call it OET prep?' as a counsel question with a real chance of 'no'.

variants._note: Listening and Reading are identical for all professions; Writing and Speaking are profession-specific. This is the single biggest content-cost fact about OET: 2 shared banks + 2 x N profession-specific banks. Launch scope is nursing only.

components.label: Writing
components._subskill_todo: OET publishes analytic assessment criteria for Writing. They are NOT reproduced here because they were not verified against a primary CBLA source in this pass. Do not invent them. Confirm from the OET Assessor guidelines before populating.

components.label: Speaking
components._subskill_todo: OET Speaking is assessed on both linguistic and clinical-communication criteria. NOT reproduced here — unverified. Confirm from primary source before populating.
components._delivery_note: delivery is 'roleplay', which the frontend has reserved as a SpeakingFormat enum value but has never built. This is real new UI, not a config change.

overall._critical: OET DOES NOT ISSUE AN OVERALL GRADE. Confirmed three ways in CBLA's own materials: the Test Regulations ('An overall grade for the OET Test is not issued'), the results page ('There is no overall grade for the OET Test'), and the statistics page ('OET does not report overall scores or grades'). Any headline 'OET score' is an invention. This is why overall.mode exists — see EE-00 §2.1. Regulators set requirements per sub-test precisely because no aggregate exists.
overall._regulator_targets_note: Because requirements are per sub-test, the target model for OET is a per-component target (e.g. B in Listening, Reading, Speaking; C+ in Writing for the NMC), not a single headline target.

target._preset_note: Regulator requirements change. These are config, so they update without a deploy — but they must be re-verified against each regulator before launch and reviewed at least annually.

progression._note: Per-component progression only. There is no headline rung to climb.

legal._policy_note: ETS publishes an explicit third-party trademark policy — this is the most workable of the three restricted marks. It requires the exact attribution above, forbids use of ETS marks in company, domain or product names, forbids ETS logos, and requires materials to be submitted to trademarks@ets.org for review (roughly 10 business days). Build the review step into the launch checklist, not after.

components.label: Verbal Reasoning
components._structure: Two sections: 12 questions / 18 min, then 15 questions / 23 min. Section-level adaptive — the second section's difficulty depends on performance in the first.
components._reuse: modality 'reading' — reuses the existing passage/item runner. No new UI.

components.label: Quantitative Reasoning
components._structure: Two sections: 12 questions / 21 min, then 15 questions / 26 min. Section-level adaptive. On-screen calculator provided.
components._new_build: delivery 'quantitative_item_set' does NOT exist. This needs a real item renderer — maths notation, figures, quantitative-comparison answer layout, calculator. This is the honest cost of GRE: config covers everything except this.

components.label: Analytical Writing
components._structure: One 'Analyze an Issue' task, 30 minutes, always presented first. The 'Analyze an Argument' task was retired with the shortened format.
components._reuse: modality 'writing' — reuses the existing essay runner.

overall._critical: ETS reports three scores and NO combined score. The Guide to the Use of Scores instructs users to 'Consider Verbal Reasoning, Quantitative Reasoning and Analytical Writing Scores as Three Separate and Independent Measures.' The widely quoted 260–340 'GRE total' is third parties summing V+Q; ETS does not compute, report or endorse it, and it discards Analytical Writing entirely.

unofficial_aggregate.label: V+Q (unofficial)
unofficial_aggregate._note: Present but DISABLED. If ever enabled it must render with the word 'unofficial' adjacent, must never be called a 'total', and must never be the headline. Enabling it is a product decision with a truthfulness cost.

rules._reliability_reference: ETS publishes reliability and SEM for the shortened test: Verbal reliability 0.88 / SEM 3.17; Quantitative 0.94 / SEM 2.56; Analytical Writing 0.77 / SEM 0.40. Use these as the denominator for any calibration claim on GRE — see TC-09.

gmat._prisma_enum_warning: GMAT IS NOT IN THE CURRENT PRISMA ExamType ENUM (IELTS, SPOKEN, OET, GRE, TOEFL, PTE). Registering this exam therefore requires a schema migration — which is precisely the 'config-only, zero code change' promise failing on the very first new exam. See EE-00 §4.1.

components.label: Quantitative Reasoning
components._new_build: Same missing renderer as GRE Quant. Build once, both exams use it.

components.label: Verbal Reasoning
components._reuse: Reuses the existing passage/item runner. Sentence Correction was retired with the Focus Edition — do not build it.

components.label: Data Insights
components._new_build: The most expensive component in this config. Sortable tables, multi-tab source panels, chart interpretation, two-part answer grids — five distinct interaction patterns with no existing analogue in the platform.

overall._critical: A GMAT Total Score exists (205–805, in 10s, always ending in 5) but THIS ENGINE MUST NEVER COMPUTE IT. GMAC does not publish the formula; it is a proprietary scaled composite of three IRT-scaled section scores. GMAC states only that the three sections are 'weighted equally'. It is demonstrably not a sum or mean — three sections of 60–90 sum to 180–270 and average to 60–90, and neither maps to 205–805. The scale is declared so that a real, student-entered GMAT score can be stored and displayed. Practice results report per component only.
overall._no_estimate: Do not ship an 'estimated GMAT total'. Any number we invent would be presented next to a real, well-known scale and read as a prediction of it. That is the single clearest way to make a calibration claim we cannot defend.

rules._edition_note: The current exam is the GMAT Focus Edition, live since 1 February 2024, replacing the 10th Edition. It has no Analytical Writing Assessment and no Integrated Reasoning section. Focus and 10th Edition scores are not directly comparable; GMAC publishes concordance tables. Any legacy content written to the old structure is unusable.
